Docker's been a game-changer since 2013, but how does it actually work under the hood?

Here's the core insight: containers aren't tiny virtual machines. They're lightweight processes that share your OS kernel while staying completely isolated from each other using Linux namespaces and cgroups.

This is why a container weighs ~5-15MB and starts in ~50ms, while a VM needs 2GB and 3-5 minutes. You can run 50+ containers on hardware that'd barely handle 3-4 VMs.

The practical payoff? Your app works identically on your laptop, your colleague's machine, and production. That's why 13 million developers have adopted Docker.

New to containers or want to understand the architecture behind the technology you use daily? This guide breaks it down without the jargon.
